    (hn : star v ⬝ᵥ v = 1) : (starRingEnd ℂ) (v h) * v h + (starRingEnd ℂ) (v k) * v k = 1

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_47
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_47 :
    (∀ (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (h : ι → ℝ) (X Y : Matrix ι ι ℝ), h ⬝ᵥ h = 1 → Xᵀ = -X →
      Yᵀ = -Y → massFormLine h X Y = 2 * ((X *ᵥ h) ⬝ᵥ (Y *ᵥ h))) ∧
    (∀ (v : Fin 5 → ℂ) (X Y : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℂ), star v ⬝ᵥ v = 1 → Xᴴ = -X → Yᴴ = -Y →
      massFormLine (realVec v) (realify X) (realify Y) = 2 * (star (X *ᵥ v) ⬝ᵥ (Y *ᵥ v)).re) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ v : Fin 5 → ℂ, (∀ a, a ≠ h → a ≠ k → v a = 0) → star v ⬝ᵥ v = 1 →
      ∃ T : Fin 13 → Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℂ,
      (∀ j, T j ∈ blockTurns {h, k}) ∧
      (∀ Z ∈ blockTurns {h, k}, Z ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range T)) ∧
      (∀ i j, ((T i)ᴴ * T j).trace.re = if i = j then 1 else 0) ∧
      (∀ i j, (star (T i *ᵥ v) ⬝ᵥ (T j *ᵥ v)).re = if i = j then w13 i else 0)) ∧
    ((Finset.univ.filter fun j => w13Z j ≠ 0).card = 3 ∧ (∀ j, w13 j = (w13Z j : ℝ) / norm13 j) ∧
      (3 : ℚ) / 13 * (1 - 3 / 13) = 30 / 169) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ v : Fin 5 → ℂ, (∀ a, a ≠ h → a ≠ k → v a = 0) → star v ⬝ᵥ v = 1 →
      ∃ T : Fin 12 → Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℂ,
      (∀ j, T j ∈ blockTurns0 {h, k}) ∧
      (∀ Z ∈ blockTurns0 {h, k}, Z ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range T)) ∧
      (∀ i j, ((T i)ᴴ * T j).trace.re = if i = j then 1 else 0) ∧
      (Matrix.of fun i j => (star (T i *ᵥ v) ⬝ᵥ (T j *ᵥ v)).re).charpoly =
        X ^ 9 * (X - C (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ^ 2 * (X - C (4 / 5 : ℝ))) ∧
    ((1 / 2 : ℝ) / (4 / 5) = 5 / 8 ∧ 1 - (1 / 2 : ℝ) / (4 / 5) = 3 / 8)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 47 (the last-step direction).** The mass form of the division of a real line is `M_h(X, Y) = 2⟨Xh, Yh⟩`, on
`ℂ⁵ = ℝ¹⁰` `M_v(X, Y) = 2 Re⟨Xv, Yv⟩` for anti-Hermitian `X`, `Y`, so `M_v(X, X) = 2|Xv|²`, and `½M_v` is the
Gram `Re⟨Xv, Yv⟩`; for every plane `F = {h, k}` and every unit vector `v`
of `F`: thirteen rotations that span `u(3) ⊕ u(2)` (the anti-Hermitian matrices with no entry across `F`), orthonormal
for `Re tr(X†Y)`, on which `½M_v(X_i, X_j) = Re⟨X_iv, X_jv⟩ = diag(1, 0, ½, ½, 0, …, 0)`: three of thirteen move
the last-step direction, `w_h = 3/13`, `χ_h = w_h(1 − w_h) = 30/169`; and twelve orthonormal rotations that span `s(u(3) ⊕ u(2))`, on
which the form has `det(x − G) = x⁹(x − ½)²(x − 4/5)`: `½M_v = 4/5, ½, ½, 0⁹`; `(½)/(4/5) = 5/8`,
`sin²θ = 1 − 5/8 = 3/8`.

Recognition: the last-step direction moves `W⁺`, `W⁻` and `Z` (`½, ½, 4/5`); nine stay massless, the photon and the eight colour
rotations; the last-step direction's length is the Higgs scalar; at the source `M_W²/M_Z² = 5/8`, `sin²θ_W = 3/8`. Uses Props. 21, 39,
46, Definition 27.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.ell_eq_rel
theorems.statement: theorem ell_eq_rel (t : Fin 5) : ell t = rel (lineIdx t)

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.ell_eq_iff
theorems.statement: theorem ell_eq_iff (s t : Fin 5) : ell s = ell t ↔ s = t
theorems.description: Two vector states are equal exactly when their lines are.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_24
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_24 :
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, (∃ c : ℂ, γ s * γ t = c • (1 : Matrix Four Four ℂ)) ↔ s = t) ∧
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, ell s = ell t ↔ s = t) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), w.IsChain (fun s t => ell s ≠ ell t) ↔ IsHistory w) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), ∃! w' : List (Fin 5), Relation.ReflTransGen Cancel w w' ∧ IsHistory w') ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, ((words (n + 1)).filter IsHistory).card = 5 * 4 ^ n)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 24 (a walk is a reduced word).** `γ_sγ_t` is a number exactly when `s = t`; the step `s`
changes the two-spinor state to its own previous moment, `ℓ_t`, exactly when `s ≠ t`, so the words in which every step changes
that two-spinor state (P5 (b)) are the reduced words, the walks; every word reduces to exactly one reduced word by
removing pairs `tt`; there are `5·4ⁿ⁻¹` walks of length `n ≥ 1` (here `n + 1`, `5·4ⁿ`).

Recognition: none (each walk has four continuations, Prop. 26). Uses Props. 4, 10. Every candidate system:
`System.uniqueness`.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.Sw_eq
theorems.statement: theorem Sw_eq (w : List (Fin 5)) : Sw w = w.foldr (fun t S => symmDiff S (Finset.univ.erase t)) ∅

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.Sw_append
theorems.statement: theorem Sw_append (u v : List (Fin 5)) : Sw (u ++ v) = symmDiff (Sw u) (Sw v)

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.relLine_eq
theorems.statement: theorem relLine_eq (w : List (Fin 5)) : relLine w = (coef w : ℂ) • rel (relOfWord w)

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.coef_values
theorems.statement: theorem coef_values (w : List (Fin 5)) : coef w = 1 ∨ coef w = -1

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.disagreeSet_eq_empty_iff
theorems.statement: theorem disagreeSet_eq_empty_iff (k : Fin 16) : disagreeSet k = ∅ ↔ k = 0

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.even_disagreeSet
theorems.statement: theorem even_disagreeSet (k : Fin 16) : Even (disagreeSet k).card

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.exists_disagreeSet
theorems.statement: theorem exists_disagreeSet (S : Finset (Fin 5)) (hS : Even S.card) : ∃ k : Fin 16, disagreeSet k = S

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.adjacency_character
theorems.statement:
theorem adjacency_character (l : Fin 16) :
    (A ℤ) *ᵥ (fun k => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (disagreeSet l ∩ disagreeSet k).card) =
      (5 - 2 * ((disagreeSet l).card : ℤ)) • fun k => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (disagreeSet l ∩ disagreeSet k).card
theorems.description: The adjacency on a character: `A χ_l = (5 − 2|T_l|) χ_l`, `χ_l(k) = (−1)^{|T_l ∩ T_k|}`.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_25
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_25 :
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), relLine w = (coef w : ℂ) • rel (relOfWord w) ∧ (coef w = 1 ∨ coef w = -1) ∧
      disagreeSet (relOfWord w) = Sw w) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), AtOnePlace (relLine w) ↔ Sw w = ∅) ∧
    (∀ u v : List (Fin 5), Sw (u ++ v) = symmDiff (Sw u) (Sw v)) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 5), (∃ w : List (Fin 5), Sw w = S) ↔ Even S.card) ∧
    (∀ (s : Fin 5) (k : Fin 16), disagreeSet (transition s k) = symmDiff (disagreeSet k) (T s)) ∧
    (∀ k : Fin 16, (Finset.univ.filter (Adjacent k)).card = 5) ∧
    (∀ k l : Fin 16, k ≠ l → (Finset.univ.filter fun m => Adjacent k m ∧ Adjacent l m).card =
      if Adjacent k l then 0 else 2) ∧
    (∀ l : Fin 16, (A ℤ) *ᵥ (fun k => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (disagreeSet l ∩ disagreeSet k).card) =
      (5 - 2 * ((disagreeSet l).card : ℤ)) • fun k => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (disagreeSet l ∩ disagreeSet k).card)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 25 (the vertices of a line).** The two-spinor state between two moments of a line is `r = ±e_S`, with
`S = T_{t_k} △ ⋯ △ T_{t_{j+1}}` the parities of the steps between them; the two moments are at one vertex exactly
when `S = ∅`; the sets compose, `S(j,k) △ S(k,l) = S(j,l)`; they are exactly the sixteen even sets of lines, so
fixing a moment labels the vertices by the sixteen sets, and another moment adds one set to every label; a step along
`s` takes `x` to `x ⊕ g_s`, `g_s = T_s`; the five steps lead from each vertex to five vertices, as the Clebsch graph
(five neighbours, none in common for two neighbours, two otherwise); the adjacency `A` has the eigenvalue
`5 − 2|U|` on the character `χ_U(x) = (−1)^{|U ∩ x|}`.

Recognition: the vertices are positions relative to one another only; there is no origin. Uses Props. 10, 14.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_26
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_26 :
    Fintype.card State = 80 ∧
    (∀ s' s : State, B ℚ s' s = if s'.2 ≠ s.2 ∧ s'.1 = transition s'.2 s.1 then 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ s : State, undoState s = (transition s.2 s.1, s.2)) ∧
    (∀ s' s : State, undoR s' s = if s' = undoState s then 1 else 0) ∧
    undoR * undoR = 1 ∧
    (∀ s : State, (Finset.univ.filter (Continues s)).card = 4) ∧
    (∀ s' : State, (Finset.univ.filter fun s => Continues s s').card = 4) ∧
    (∑ s' : State, ∑ s : State, B ℚ s' s) = 320 ∧
    (∀ s' s : State, (B ℚ + undoR) s' s = if s'.1 = transition s'.2 s.1 then 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ s : State, (Finset.univ.filter fun s' : State => s'.1 = transition s'.2 s.1).card = 5)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 26 (eighty states and four continuations).** The state of a line is its two-spinor state and its last-step direction,
`(x, t)`: eighty states; the step is `B(x′, s; x, t) = [s ≠ t][x′ = x ⊕ g_s]` and the undo
`R(x, t) = (x ⊕ g_t, t)`, `R² = 1`; every state has four continuations and four predecessors, `320` arcs; `B + R`
takes each state to its five neighbours, `(B + R)(x′, s; x, t) = [x′ = x ⊕ g_s]`.

Recognition: the two-spinor states and their steps are the cells of `ℝP⁴` (Prop. 38, SI Prop. 116). Uses Props. 24, 25.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.T_succ
theorems.statement: theorem T_succ (h : Fin 5) : (T h).map (Fin.succEmb 5) = Finset.univ.erase 0 \ {h.succ}
theorems.description: The division of the six reversed by `γ_h ⊗ γ_h` and by the plane, as sets of directions.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_27
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_27 (h k' : Fin 5) (hk : h ≠ k') :
    relLine [] = Ω ∧
    relLine [h] = ell h ∧ ell h = rel (lineIdx h) ∧ disagreeSet (lineIdx h) = T h ∧
    (relLine [h, k'] = (coef [h, k'] : ℂ) • rel (relOfWord [h, k']) ∧ (coef [h, k'] = 1 ∨ coef [h, k'] = -1) ∧
      disagreeSet (relOfWord [h, k']) = {h, k'}) ∧
    (∀ c : Fin 6, γ h * sixP1 c * (γ h)ᵀ = thetaAt ((T h).map (Fin.succEmb 5)) c • sixP1 c ∧
      thetaAt ((T h).map (Fin.succEmb 5)) c = -thetaAt {0, h.succ} c) ∧
    (∀ c : Fin 6, (γ h * γ k') * sixP1 c * (γ h * γ k')ᵀ = thetaAt {h.succ, k'.succ} c • sixP1 c) ∧
    dividedSet 0 = ∅ ∧ dividedSet (lineIdx h) = {0, h.succ} ∧ dividedSet (relOfWord [h, k']) = {h.succ, k'.succ} ∧
    twin ∅ = {0} ∧ twin {0, h.succ} = {h.succ} ∧
      twin {h.succ, k'.succ} = (({h, k'} : Finset (Fin 5))ᶜ).map (Fin.succEmb 5) ∧
    [linesDivided ∅, linesDivided {0, h.succ}, linesDivided {h.succ, k'.succ}, linesDivided {0},
      linesDivided {h.succ}, linesDivided ((({h, k'} : Finset (Fin 5))ᶜ).map (Fin.succEmb 5))] =
      [0, 4, 2, 5, 1, 3]
theorems.description:
**Proposition 27 (what a line holds).** With `h` the last-step direction and `k′` the step before it (`h ≠ k′`):
`r_{k,k} = Ω`, `r_{k,k−1} = ℓ_h = e_{T_h}`, `r_{k,k−2} = ±e_{h k′}`; on P1's real six
`γ_h ⊗ γ_h = θ_{T_h} = −θ_{\{h,n\}}` and `γ_hγ_{k′} ⊗ γ_hγ_{k′} = θ_{\{h,k′\}}`; the divided sets of the three two-spinor states
are `{}`, `{h, n}`, `F = {h, k′}`, their counterparts `{n}`, `{h}`, `C` (the three lines outside `F`), and these are the six
divisions of Prop. 22 with the singlet fixed, each once: they divide `0, 4, 2, 5, 1, 3` lines.

Recognition: the line holds its own time `{h, n}`, its own direction `{h}`, its clock plane `F` and the three lines
outside it. Uses Props. 10, 22, 24, Definitions 18, 29.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.sigma5_apply
theorems.statement: theorem sigma5_apply (i j : Fin 5) : sigma5 i j = if i = j then -3 / 5 else 2 / 5

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.sigma5_eq_coin
theorems.statement: theorem sigma5_eq_coin (i j : Fin 5) : sigma5 i j = (coin i j : ℝ)

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.involutions_real
theorems.statement:
theorem involutions_real (a b : ℝ) :
    (a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)))ᵀ *
        (a • 1 + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ))) = 1 ↔
      (a = 1 ∧ b = 0) ∨ (a = -1 ∧ b = 0) ∨ (a = -1 ∧ b = 2 / 5) ∨ (a = 1 ∧ b = -2 / 5)
theorems.description: **The involutions made of `1` and `𝟏𝟏ᵀ` over the real numbers.**

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.sigma5_eq_comb
theorems.statement:
theorem sigma5_eq_comb : sigma5 = (-1 : ℝ) • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) +
    (2 / 5 : ℝ) • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ))

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_28
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_28 :
    (∀ a b : ℝ, (a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)))ᵀ *
        (a • 1 + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ))) = 1 →
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) ≠ 1 →
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) ≠ -1 →
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) = sigma5 ∨
        a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) = -sigma5) ∧
    (∀ X : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ, (∀ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin 5), X.submatrix π π = X) →
      ∃ a b : ℝ, X = a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ))) ∧
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, sigma5 s t = if s = t then -3 / 5 else 2 / 5) ∧
    sigma5 * sigma5 = 1 ∧
    (∀ t : Fin 5, (∑ s, sigma5 s t ^ 2 = 1) ∧ (∑ s, ((sigma5 s t : ℝ) : ℂ) • γ s) = gamma (fun s => sigma5 s t) ∧
      gamma (fun s => sigma5 s t) * gamma (fun s => sigma5 s t) = 1) ∧
    stepU = (2 / 5 : ℚ) • B ℚ - (3 / 5 : ℚ) • undoR ∧ stepUᵀ * stepU = 1
theorems.description:
**Proposition 28 (the coin).** A real `X = aI + b𝟏𝟏ᵀ` with `XᵀX = I` and `X ≠ ±I` is `±σ₅`,
`σ₅ = (2/5)𝟏𝟏ᵀ − I`; a real matrix that no relabelling of the five directions changes is of that form, so `±σ₅` are the
only orthogonal involutions besides `±1` that no relabelling changes; `(σ₅)_{tt} = −3/5`, `(σ₅)_{st} = 2/5`,
`σ₅² = I`; the step from the last-step direction `t` is the line `γ(x_t)`, `x_t = (2/5)𝟏 − e_t` the column of `σ₅`, of length one,
`γ(x_t)² = 1`; on the eighty states `U = (2/5)B − (3/5)R` and `UᵀU = I`.

Recognition: the radar echo of one step, `(3/5)² + 4(2/5)² = 1 = v² + 1/γ²` with `v = 3/5`, `γ = 5/4`. Uses
Props. 4, 26, P1, P2 (a), P3 (b).

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.between_zero_succ_steps
theorems.statement: theorem between_zero_succ_steps (t : Steps) (n : ℕ) : between t 0 (n + 1) = t n :: between t 0 n
theorems.description: The first `n + 1` steps: the step `t n` before the first `n`.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.relAt_eq_relation_of_word
theorems.statement: theorem relAt_eq_relation_of_word (t : Steps) (n : ℕ) : relAt t n = relationOf (between t 0 n)
theorems.description: **P5 (c) on the words:** the two-spinor state at the moment `n` is the two-spinor state of the word of the first `n` steps.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.changesEachStep_iff_histories
theorems.statement: theorem changesEachStep_iff_histories (t : Steps) : ChangesEachStep t ↔ ∀ n, IsHistory (between t 0 n)
theorems.description:
**P5 (b) makes the walks:** a sequence of steps changes its two-spinor state at each step exactly when each of its
first segments is a walk.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_24_full
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_24_full :
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, (∃ c : ℂ, γ s * γ t = c • (1 : Matrix Four Four ℂ)) ↔ s = t) ∧
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, ell s = ell t ↔ s = t) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), w.IsChain (fun s t => ell s ≠ ell t) ↔ IsHistory w) ∧
    (∀ t : Steps, ChangesEachStep t ↔ ∀ n, IsHistory (between t 0 n)) ∧
    (∀ (t : Steps) (n : ℕ), relAt t n = relationOf (between t 0 n)) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), ∃! w' : List (Fin 5), Relation.ReflTransGen Cancel w w' ∧ IsHistory w') ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, ((words (n + 1)).filter IsHistory).card = 5 * 4 ^ n)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 24 (a walk is a reduced word).** `γ_sγ_t` is a number exactly when `s = t`; the step `s`
changes the two-spinor state to its own previous moment, `ℓ_t`, exactly when `s ≠ t`, so the words in which every step changes
that two-spinor state (P5 (b)) are the reduced words, the walks; a line's steps (P5 (a)) change the two-spinor state at each step
exactly when every first segment of them is a walk, and its two-spinor state at the moment `n` is the two-spinor state of the
word of its first `n` steps (P5 (c)); every word reduces to exactly one reduced word by removing pairs `tt`; there
are `5·4ⁿ⁻¹` walks of length `n ≥ 1` (here `n + 1`, `5·4ⁿ`).

Recognition: none (each walk has four continuations, Prop. 26). Uses Props. 4, 10, P5 (a), (b), (c).

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_45
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_45 (h k : Fin 5) (hk : h ≠ k) :
    (∀ r : Fin 16, nPlane h k r + nOut h k r = (disagreeSet r).card ∧
      ((disagreeSet r).card = 0 ∨ (disagreeSet r).card = 2 ∨ (disagreeSet r).card = 4)) ∧
    ((Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 0 ∧ nOut h k r = 0).card = 1 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 2 ∧ nOut h k r = 0).card = 1 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 1 ∧ nOut h k r = 1).card = 6 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 0 ∧ nOut h k r = 2).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 1 ∧ nOut h k r = 3).card = 2 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 2 ∧ nOut h k r = 2).card = 3) ∧
    (∀ r : Fin 16,
      (nPlane h k r = 0 ∧ nOut h k r = 0 → hyper h k r = 0) ∧
      (nPlane h k r = 2 ∧ nOut h k r = 0 → hyper h k r = 1) ∧
      (nPlane h k r = 1 ∧ nOut h k r = 1 → hyper h k r = 1 / 6) ∧
      (nPlane h k r = 0 ∧ nOut h k r = 2 → hyper h k r = -2 / 3) ∧
      (nPlane h k r = 1 ∧ nOut h k r = 3 → hyper h k r = -1 / 2) ∧
      (nPlane h k r = 2 ∧ nOut h k r = 2 → hyper h k r = 1 / 3)) ∧
    (∀ r : Fin 16, hyper h k r = ∑ x ∈ disagreeSet r, lineY h k x) ∧ ∑ x, lineY h k x = 0 ∧
    ((Finset.univ.filter fun r => hyper h k r = 0).card = 1 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => hyper h k r = 1 / 6).card = 6 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => hyper h k r = -2 / 3).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => hyper h k r = 1).card = 1 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => hyper h k r = 1 / 3).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => hyper h k r = -1 / 2).card = 2) ∧
    (∑ r, hyper h k r = 0 ∧ ∑ r, hyper h k r ^ 3 = 0 ∧
     ∑ r ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun r => nOut h k r = 1 ∨ nOut h k r = 2), hyper h k r = 0 ∧
     ∑ r ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun r => nPlane h k r = 1), hyper h k r = 0 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nOut h k r = 1).card = (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nOut h k r = 2).card ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => nPlane h k r = 1).card = 8) ∧
    ∑ r, hyper h k r ^ 5 = 5 / 9 ∧
    (∀ r : Fin 16, charge h k r = isospin h k r + hyper h k r) ∧
    (∀ r : Fin 16, isospin h k r =
      ((if k ∈ disagreeSet r then 1 else 0) - (if h ∈ disagreeSet r then 1 else 0)) / 2) ∧
    ((Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = 0).card = 2 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = 2 / 3).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = -1 / 3).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = -2 / 3).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = 1 / 3).card = 3 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = 1).card = 1 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => charge h k r = -1).card = 1) ∧
    (charge h k (transition h 0) = 0 ∧ charge h k (transition k 0) = -1) ∧
    ((Finset.univ.filter fun r => (disagreeSet r).card = 2 ∧ nPlane h k r = 2).card = 1 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => (disagreeSet r).card = 2 ∧ nPlane h k r = 1).card = 6 ∧
     (Finset.univ.filter fun r => (disagreeSet r).card = 2 ∧ nPlane h k r = 0).card = 3)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 45 (one generation, seen from the plane).** For every plane `F = {h, k}`: each two-spinor state `e_S`
meets the plane in `N_F = |S ∩ F|` lines and the outside in `N_C = |S ∩ C|`, `N_F + N_C = |S| ∈ {0, 2, 4}`; the
classes `(N_F, N_C) = (0,0), (2,0), (1,1), (0,2), (1,3), (2,2)` hold `1, 1, 6, 3, 2, 3` two-spinor states, with
`Y = N_F/2 − N_C/3 = 0, 1, 1/6, −2/3, −1/2, 1/3`; `Y = Σ_{x ∈ S} y_x` with `y = ½` on the plane and `−⅓` outside,
`Σ_x y_x = 0`; the values of `Y` occur `1, 6, 3, 1, 3, 2` times; `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, the colour and the doublet sums of
`Y` vanish, as many two-spinor states in triplets as in antitriplets, eight in doublets; `Σ Y⁵ = 5/9`;
`Q = N_k − N_C/3 = T₃ + Y`, `T₃ = (N_k − N_h)/2`, with the charges `0` twice, `2/3, −1/3, −2/3, 1/3` three times,
`±1` once; the last-step direction's vector state is neutral; the ten symmetric states meet `F` in two lines once, in one line six times, in
none three times.

Recognition: with the line charges `(0, 1, −⅓, −⅓, −⅓)` the sixteen two-spinor states are `ν^c` (`Y = 0`), `e^c` (`1`),
`u^c` (`−2/3`, three), `Q` (`1/6`, six), `d^c` (`1/3`, three) and `L` (`−1/2`, two): one generation with its
right-handed neutrino; the vanishing sums are the absence of anomalies; the eight two-spinor states meeting the plane in one
line are the weak doublets, parity broken at the plane. Uses Props. 10, 25.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_48_irreps
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_48_irreps :
    (∀ k : Fin 16, (disagreeSet k).card = 0 ∨ (disagreeSet k).card = 2 ∨ (disagreeSet k).card = 4) ∧
    (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin 16 => (disagreeSet k).card = 0).card = 1 ∧
    (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin 16 => (disagreeSet k).card = 2).card = 10 ∧
    (Finset.univ.filter fun k : Fin 16 => (disagreeSet k).card = 4).card = 5 ∧
    (∀ k : Fin 16, (disagreeSet k).card ≠ 6) ∧
    (∀ k : Fin 16, L *ᵥ rel k = ((Lvalue k : ℤ) : ℂ) • rel k ∧ Lvalue k = 6 - 2 * (disagreeSet k).card) ∧
    (∀ k : Fin 16,
      ((1 / 4 : ℂ) • Eop) *ᵥ rel k = (if (disagreeSet k).card = 0 then 1 else 0 : ℂ) • rel k ∧
      ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 + swap)) *ᵥ rel k = (if (disagreeSet k).card = 2 then 1 else 0 : ℂ) • rel k ∧
      ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 - swap) - (1 / 4 : ℂ) • Eop) *ᵥ rel k =
        (if (disagreeSet k).card = 4 then 1 else 0 : ℂ) • rel k)
theorems.description:
Proposition 48, the singlet, symmetric and vector states and their projectors (`IrrepsWhole.lean`: `prop_48`). A two-spinor state disagrees on `N = 0`, `2` or `4` lines, `1 + 10 + 5` two-spinor states,
and none on six (an even set of five lines has at most four); the comparison is `L = 6 − 2N = 6, 2, −2` on them;
`Π₀ = E/4`, `Π_F = (1 + P)/2`, `Π_L = (1 − P)/2 − E/4` are one on the singlet, the symmetric states and the vector states
respectively and zero on the others.

Recognition: three families and no fourth, the electron at no distinction, the muon reaching the symmetric states, the tau
reaching the vector states. Uses Props. 10, 11, 13.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_49
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_49 (a b : Fin 5) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    zS {a.succ, b.succ} = -1 ∧ Law.LS {a.succ, b.succ} = 5 ∧ Law.wS {a.succ, b.succ} = -1 / 5 ∧
    Law.wS {a.succ, b.succ} ^ 2 = 1 / 25 ∧
    zS (outside a b) = -I ∧ Law.LS (outside a b) = -1 ∧ Law.wS (outside a b) = I ∧
    Law.wS (outside a b) ^ 2 = -1 ∧
    (∀ z : ℂ, Law.Phi z = -z ^ 2 * Law.Psi (z ^ 2 / 16)) ∧ (∀ v : ℂ, Law.Psi v = v / (1 + 3 * v)) ∧
    Law.PsiS {a.succ, b.succ} = 1 / 28 ∧ Law.PsiS (outside a b) = 1 / 2 ∧
    zS {a.succ, b.succ} ^ 2 = 1 ∧ zS (outside a b) ^ 2 = -1 ∧
    (∀ k : Fin 16, k ≠ 0 → |(Lvalue k : ℝ) / 6| = 1 / 3 ∧ Real.sqrt (|(Lvalue k : ℝ) / 6|)⁻¹ = Real.sqrt 3)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 49 (one plane at its two signs).** For every plane `{a, b}`: at the plane itself (even, a count)
`z = −1`, `L = 5`, `w = −1/5`, `w² = 1/25`; at its counterpart `{a, b}'`, the three lines outside it (odd, an amplitude),
`z = −i`, `L = −1`, `w = i`, `w² = −1`; `Φ(z) = −z²Ψ(z²/16)` with `Ψ(v) = v/(1 + 3v)`; `Ψ(w²) = 1/28` at the plane and
`1/2` at its counterpart with `n` added; the sign `z²` each puts on the clock is `+1`, `−1`; on both signs each two-spinor state of the singlet, the symmetric or the vector states weighs
`|L/6|^{−1/2} = √3`.

Recognition: the charged leptons sit at the plane and the quarks at its counterpart with `n` added, one mass operator for both. Uses
Props. 10, 30, 44.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.b_value

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_50
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_50 (a b : Fin 5) (hab : a ≠ b) :
    ((varP / (2 * (varP + varQ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) + Law.wS (outside a b) = 7 / 16 + I ∧
    ((varP / (2 * (varP + varQ)) : ℝ) : ℂ) + Law.wS {0, a.succ, b.succ} = 7 / 16 - I ∧
    Complex.arg (7 / 16 + I) = Complex.arg (7 + 16 * I) ∧
    Complex.arg (7 + 16 * I) = Real.arctan (16 / 7) ∧
    ((1.158385 : ℝ) < Complex.arg (7 + 16 * I) ∧ Complex.arg (7 + 16 * I) < 1.158395) ∧
    Complex.arg (7 / 16 - I) = -Complex.arg (7 + 16 * I)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 50 (the complex weight).** For every plane `{a, b}`: the plane whose one end counts an excursion at `{}`,
`b = Var P/(2(Var P + Var Q)) = 7/16` (Prop. 30), and whose other end carries the three outside lines,
`w_C = i` (Prop. 44), has `b + w_C = 7/16 + i`, of angle `arg(7 + 16i) = arctan(16/7) = 1.15839…`; with the other
orientation of the square root of the sign (`C` named `{n, a, b}`, `w = −i`), `b + w = 7/16 − i`, of angle `−arg(7 + 16i)`.

Recognition: the phase of quark mixing and its sign; the orientation `q` is the one that calls matter matter. Uses
Props. 30, 44.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_51
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_51 :
    Article.lineFactor (1 / 4) = 2 ∧ Article.lineFactor (I / 4) = 3 / 4 * (1 + I) ∧
    Complex.arg (Article.lineFactor (I / 4)) = Real.pi / 4 ∧
    Real.tan (Real.pi / 8) ^ 2 = 3 - 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ∧
    ((0.1715725 : ℝ) < 3 - 2 * Real.sqrt 2 ∧ 3 - 2 * Real.sqrt 2 < 0.1715735) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 6), Even S.card →
      (Article.lineFactor (Law.uS S)).im = 0 ∧ 0 < (Article.lineFactor (Law.uS S)).re) ∧
    (∀ t : Fin 5, Law.uS {t.succ} = I / 4) ∧ Law.uS ∅ = 1 / 4
theorems.description:
**Proposition 51 (the line factor at the last-step direction's phase).** The factor of the law on the vector states,
`1 + 3u + 4u²` at `u = z/4`: `2` at `z = 1` (`u_∅ = 1/4`) and `(3/4)(1 + i)` at the last-step direction's phase `z = i`
(`u_{\{t\}} = i/4`), of phase `π/4`, half phase `π/8`; `tan²(π/8) = 3 − 2√2 = 0.171573…`; at every even divided set
the factor is real and positive.

Recognition: the ratio of the two light neutral masses `ρ_ν = tan²(π/8)`. Uses Props. 35, 44.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_99
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_99 :
    (∀ h : Fin 5, (WholePicture.pairingsBeside h).card = 3) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ c ∈ outLines h k,
      Kc k c * Kc k c = -1 ∧ Kc k c * γ h = γ h * Kc k c ∧ Kc k c * sideQ h = sideQ h * Kc k c) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ c ∈ outLines h k, ∀ d ∈ outLines h k, c ≠ d →
      Kc k c * Kc k d = -(Kc k d * Kc k c)) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ X : Matrix Four Four ℂ, sideQ h * X * sideQ h = X →
      X = (1 / 2 * X.trace) • sideQ h - ∑ c ∈ outLines h k, (1 / 2 * (Kc k c * X).trace) • (Kc k c * sideQ h)) ∧
    (∀ h a b c d : Fin 5, a ≠ b → a ≠ c → a ≠ d → b ≠ c → b ≠ d → c ≠ d → a ≠ h → b ≠ h → c ≠ h → d ≠ h →
      (γ a * γ b) * (γ c * γ d) = γ h ∨ (γ a * γ b) * (γ c * γ d) = -γ h) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k →
      (∀ x : Fin 5, x ≠ h → ∑ c ∈ outLines h k, pairVec k c x = if x = k then 3 else -1) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ outLines h k, ∀ c' ∈ outLines h k,
        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => x ≠ h), pairVec k c x * pairVec k c' x = if c = c' then 4 else 0)) ∧
    Article.gramTheta = !![1, -1 / 4, -1 / 4; -1 / 4, 1, -1 / 4; -1 / 4, -1 / 4, 1] ∧
    Article.B3ᵀ * Article.gramTheta * Article.B3 = Matrix.diagonal ![1, 10, 5] ∧ (3 : ℕ) * (1 + 10 + 5) = 48
theorems.description:
**Proposition 99 (the three pairings of the four lines beside the last-step direction).** For every last-step direction `h`: the four lines
beside it pair in exactly three ways; for every plane `{h, k}` and the three lines `c` outside it, with
`K_c = γ_kγ_c` on the last-step direction's side `Q(h)H` (`Q(h) = (1 + γ_h)/2`): `K_c² = −1`, `K_cK_d = −K_dK_c`, each `K_c` keeps
the side (it commutes with `γ_h`), and every operator of the side is `½ tr(X) Q − ½ Σ_c tr(K_cX) K_cQ`, a
combination of `Q` and the three `K_cQ`; for each pairing `{a, b | c, d}` of the four lines,
`(γ_aγ_b)(γ_cγ_d) = ±γ_h`, so on the side `γ_aγ_b = ∓γ_cγ_d`; the pairing vectors, `+1` on the pair of `k` and `−1`
on the other, are orthogonal on the four lines (`Σ_x χ_cχ_{c'} = 4δ`) and sum to `3` at `k` and `−1` at each
outside line, `(3, −1, −1, −1)`; `G_Θ = (5I − 𝖩₃)/4` on `1, −P, −E` has `B₃ᵀG_ΘB₃ = diag(1, 10, 5)`;
`3(1 + 10 + 5) = 48`.

Recognition: the three families, each one of the three ways the four lines beside the last-step direction split into two symmetric states; on
the last-step direction's doublet the same three are the three rotations of spin. Uses Props. 4, 5, 13, 48.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.irreps_from_pairings
theorems.statement:
theorem irreps_from_pairings : ∀ j : Fin 3,
    ![(1 / 4 : ℂ) • Comparison.Eop, (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 + Comparison.swap),
      (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 - Comparison.swap) - (1 / 4 : ℂ) • Comparison.Eop] j =
      (1 / 4 : ℂ) • ∑ i, Article.B3 i j • Article.XTheta i
theorems.description: **The three projectors in the basis `1, −P, −E`:** `Π_j = (1/4) Σ_i (B₃)_{ij} X_i`.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.Existence.prop_99_full
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_99_full :
    (∀ h : Fin 5, (WholePicture.pairingsBeside h).card = 3) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ c ∈ outLines h k,
      Kc k c * Kc k c = -1 ∧ Kc k c * γ h = γ h * Kc k c ∧ Kc k c * sideQ h = sideQ h * Kc k c) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ c ∈ outLines h k, ∀ d ∈ outLines h k, c ≠ d →
      Kc k c * Kc k d = -(Kc k d * Kc k c)) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → ∀ X : Matrix Four Four ℂ, sideQ h * X * sideQ h = X →
      X = (1 / 2 * X.trace) • sideQ h - ∑ c ∈ outLines h k, (1 / 2 * (Kc k c * X).trace) • (Kc k c * sideQ h)) ∧
    (∀ h a b c d : Fin 5, a ≠ b → a ≠ c → a ≠ d → b ≠ c → b ≠ d → c ≠ d → a ≠ h → b ≠ h → c ≠ h → d ≠ h →
      (γ a * γ b) * (γ c * γ d) = γ h ∨ (γ a * γ b) * (γ c * γ d) = -γ h) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k →
      (∀ x : Fin 5, x ≠ h → ∑ c ∈ outLines h k, pairVec k c x = if x = k then 3 else -1) ∧
      (∀ c ∈ outLines h k, ∀ c' ∈ outLines h k,
        ∑ x ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun x => x ≠ h), pairVec k c x * pairVec k c' x = if c = c' then 4 else 0)) ∧
    Article.gramTheta = !![1, -1 / 4, -1 / 4; -1 / 4, 1, -1 / 4; -1 / 4, -1 / 4, 1] ∧
    (∀ j : Fin 3,
      ![(1 / 4 : ℂ) • Comparison.Eop, (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 + Comparison.swap),
        (1 / 2 : ℂ) • (1 - Comparison.swap) - (1 / 4 : ℂ) • Comparison.Eop] j =
        (1 / 4 : ℂ) • ∑ i, Article.B3 i j • Article.XTheta i) ∧
    Article.B3ᵀ * Article.gramTheta * Article.B3 = Matrix.diagonal ![1, 10, 5] ∧ (3 : ℕ) * (1 + 10 + 5) = 48
theorems.description:
**Proposition 99 (the three pairings of the four lines beside the last-step direction).** For every last-step direction `h`: the four lines
beside it pair in exactly three ways; for every plane `{h, k}` and the three lines `c` outside it, with
`K_c = γ_kγ_c` on the last-step direction's side `Q(h)H` (`Q(h) = (1 + γ_h)/2`): `K_c² = −1`, `K_cK_d = −K_dK_c`, each `K_c` keeps
the side (it commutes with `γ_h`), and every operator of the side is `½ tr(X) Q − ½ Σ_c tr(K_cX) K_cQ`, a
combination of `Q` and the three `K_cQ`; for each pairing `{a, b | c, d}` of the four lines,
`(γ_aγ_b)(γ_cγ_d) = ±γ_h`, so on the side `γ_aγ_b = ∓γ_cγ_d`; the pairing vectors, `+1` on the pair of `k` and `−1`
on the other, are orthogonal on the four lines (`Σ_x χ_cχ_{c'} = 4δ`) and sum to `3` at `k` and `−1` at each
outside line, `(3, −1, −1, −1)`; `G_Θ = (5I − 𝖩₃)/4` on `X = (1, −P, −E)`; the singlet, the symmetric and the vector states `Π₀ = E/4`,
`Π_F = (1 + P)/2`, `Π_L = (1 − P)/2 − E/4` are `(1/4) Σ_i (B₃)_{ij} X_i`, so `B₃` changes one basis of the space
into the other and `B₃ᵀG_ΘB₃ = diag(1, 10, 5)` is the Gram matrix of the three projectors; `3(1 + 10 + 5) = 48`.

Recognition: the three families, each one of the three ways the four lines beside the last-step direction split into two symmetric states; on
the last-step direction's doublet the same three are the three rotations of spin. Uses Props. 4, 5, 13, 48.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_24
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_24_full :
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, (∃ c : ℂ, γ s * γ t = c • (1 : Matrix Four Four ℂ)) ↔ s = t) ∧
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, ell s = ell t ↔ s = t) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), w.IsChain (fun s t => ell s ≠ ell t) ↔ IsHistory w) ∧
    (∀ t : Steps, ChangesEachStep t ↔ ∀ n, IsHistory (between t 0 n)) ∧
    (∀ (t : Steps) (n : ℕ), relAt t n = relationOf (between t 0 n)) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), ∃! w' : List (Fin 5), Relation.ReflTransGen Cancel w w' ∧ IsHistory w') ∧
    (∀ n : ℕ, ((words (n + 1)).filter IsHistory).card = 5 * 4 ^ n)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 24 (a walk is a reduced word).** `γ_sγ_t` is a number exactly when `s = t`; the step `s`
changes the two-spinor state to its own previous moment, `ℓ_t`, exactly when `s ≠ t`, so the words in which every step changes
that two-spinor state (P5 (b)) are the reduced words, the walks; a line's steps (P5 (a)) change the two-spinor state at each step
exactly when every first segment of them is a walk, and its two-spinor state at the moment `n` is the two-spinor state of the
word of its first `n` steps (P5 (c)); every word reduces to exactly one reduced word by removing pairs `tt`; there
are `5·4ⁿ⁻¹` walks of length `n ≥ 1` (here `n + 1`, `5·4ⁿ`).

Recognition: none (each walk has four continuations, Prop. 26). Uses Props. 4, 10, P5 (a), (b), (c).

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_25
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_25 :
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), relLine w = (coef w : ℂ) • rel (relOfWord w) ∧ (coef w = 1 ∨ coef w = -1) ∧
      disagreeSet (relOfWord w) = Sw w) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), AtOnePlace (relLine w) ↔ Sw w = ∅) ∧
    (∀ u v : List (Fin 5), Sw (u ++ v) = symmDiff (Sw u) (Sw v)) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 5), (∃ w : List (Fin 5), Sw w = S) ↔ Even S.card) ∧
    (∀ (s : Fin 5) (k : Fin 16), disagreeSet (transition s k) = symmDiff (disagreeSet k) (T s)) ∧
    (∀ k : Fin 16, (Finset.univ.filter (Adjacent k)).card = 5) ∧
    (∀ k l : Fin 16, k ≠ l → (Finset.univ.filter fun m => Adjacent k m ∧ Adjacent l m).card =
      if Adjacent k l then 0 else 2) ∧
    (∀ l : Fin 16, (A ℤ) *ᵥ (fun k => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (disagreeSet l ∩ disagreeSet k).card) =
      (5 - 2 * ((disagreeSet l).card : ℤ)) • fun k => (-1 : ℤ) ^ (disagreeSet l ∩ disagreeSet k).card)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 25 (the vertices of a line).** The two-spinor state between two moments of a line is `r = ±e_S`, with
`S = T_{t_k} △ ⋯ △ T_{t_{j+1}}` the parities of the steps between them; the two moments are at one vertex exactly
when `S = ∅`; the sets compose, `S(j,k) △ S(k,l) = S(j,l)`; they are exactly the sixteen even sets of lines, so
fixing a moment labels the vertices by the sixteen sets, and another moment adds one set to every label; a step along
`s` takes `x` to `x ⊕ g_s`, `g_s = T_s`; the five steps lead from each vertex to five vertices, as the Clebsch graph
(five neighbours, none in common for two neighbours, two otherwise); the adjacency `A` has the eigenvalue
`5 − 2|U|` on the character `χ_U(x) = (−1)^{|U ∩ x|}`.

Recognition: the vertices are positions relative to one another only; there is no origin. Uses Props. 10, 14.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_26
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_26 :
    Fintype.card State = 80 ∧
    (∀ s' s : State, B ℚ s' s = if s'.2 ≠ s.2 ∧ s'.1 = transition s'.2 s.1 then 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ s : State, undoState s = (transition s.2 s.1, s.2)) ∧
    (∀ s' s : State, undoR s' s = if s' = undoState s then 1 else 0) ∧
    undoR * undoR = 1 ∧
    (∀ s : State, (Finset.univ.filter (Continues s)).card = 4) ∧
    (∀ s' : State, (Finset.univ.filter fun s => Continues s s').card = 4) ∧
    (∑ s' : State, ∑ s : State, B ℚ s' s) = 320 ∧
    (∀ s' s : State, (B ℚ + undoR) s' s = if s'.1 = transition s'.2 s.1 then 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ s : State, (Finset.univ.filter fun s' : State => s'.1 = transition s'.2 s.1).card = 5)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 26 (eighty states and four continuations).** The state of a line is its two-spinor state and its last-step direction,
`(x, t)`: eighty states; the step is `B(x′, s; x, t) = [s ≠ t][x′ = x ⊕ g_s]` and the undo
`R(x, t) = (x ⊕ g_t, t)`, `R² = 1`; every state has four continuations and four predecessors, `320` arcs; `B + R`
takes each state to its five neighbours, `(B + R)(x′, s; x, t) = [x′ = x ⊕ g_s]`.

Recognition: the two-spinor states and their steps are the cells of `ℝP⁴` (Prop. 38, SI Prop. 116). Uses Props. 24, 25.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_27
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_27 (h k' : Fin 5) (hk : h ≠ k') :
    relLine [] = Ω ∧
    relLine [h] = ell h ∧ ell h = rel (lineIdx h) ∧ disagreeSet (lineIdx h) = T h ∧
    (relLine [h, k'] = (coef [h, k'] : ℂ) • rel (relOfWord [h, k']) ∧ (coef [h, k'] = 1 ∨ coef [h, k'] = -1) ∧
      disagreeSet (relOfWord [h, k']) = {h, k'}) ∧
    (∀ c : Fin 6, γ h * sixP1 c * (γ h)ᵀ = thetaAt ((T h).map (Fin.succEmb 5)) c • sixP1 c ∧
      thetaAt ((T h).map (Fin.succEmb 5)) c = -thetaAt {0, h.succ} c) ∧
    (∀ c : Fin 6, (γ h * γ k') * sixP1 c * (γ h * γ k')ᵀ = thetaAt {h.succ, k'.succ} c • sixP1 c) ∧
    dividedSet 0 = ∅ ∧ dividedSet (lineIdx h) = {0, h.succ} ∧ dividedSet (relOfWord [h, k']) = {h.succ, k'.succ} ∧
    twin ∅ = {0} ∧ twin {0, h.succ} = {h.succ} ∧
      twin {h.succ, k'.succ} = (({h, k'} : Finset (Fin 5))ᶜ).map (Fin.succEmb 5) ∧
    [linesDivided ∅, linesDivided {0, h.succ}, linesDivided {h.succ, k'.succ}, linesDivided {0},
      linesDivided {h.succ}, linesDivided ((({h, k'} : Finset (Fin 5))ᶜ).map (Fin.succEmb 5))] =
      [0, 4, 2, 5, 1, 3]
theorems.description:
**Proposition 27 (what a line holds).** With `h` the last-step direction and `k′` the step before it (`h ≠ k′`):
`r_{k,k} = Ω`, `r_{k,k−1} = ℓ_h = e_{T_h}`, `r_{k,k−2} = ±e_{h k′}`; on P1's real six
`γ_h ⊗ γ_h = θ_{T_h} = −θ_{\{h,n\}}` and `γ_hγ_{k′} ⊗ γ_hγ_{k′} = θ_{\{h,k′\}}`; the divided sets of the three two-spinor states
are `{}`, `{h, n}`, `F = {h, k′}`, their counterparts `{n}`, `{h}`, `C` (the three lines outside `F`), and these are the six
divisions of Prop. 22 with the singlet fixed, each once: they divide `0, 4, 2, 5, 1, 3` lines.

Recognition: the line holds its own time `{h, n}`, its own direction `{h}`, its clock plane `F` and the three lines
outside it. Uses Props. 10, 22, 24, Definitions 18, 29.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_28
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_28 :
    (∀ a b : ℝ, (a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)))ᵀ *
        (a • 1 + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ))) = 1 →
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) ≠ 1 →
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) ≠ -1 →
      a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) = sigma5 ∨
        a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ)) = -sigma5) ∧
    (∀ X : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ, (∀ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin 5), X.submatrix π π = X) →
      ∃ a b : ℝ, X = a • (1 : Matrix (Fin 5) (Fin 5) ℝ) + b • Matrix.of (fun _ _ => (1 : ℝ))) ∧
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, sigma5 s t = if s = t then -3 / 5 else 2 / 5) ∧
    sigma5 * sigma5 = 1 ∧
    (∀ t : Fin 5, (∑ s, sigma5 s t ^ 2 = 1) ∧ (∑ s, ((sigma5 s t : ℝ) : ℂ) • γ s) = gamma (fun s => sigma5 s t) ∧
      gamma (fun s => sigma5 s t) * gamma (fun s => sigma5 s t) = 1) ∧
    stepU = (2 / 5 : ℚ) • B ℚ - (3 / 5 : ℚ) • undoR ∧ stepUᵀ * stepU = 1
theorems.description:
**Proposition 28 (the coin).** A real `X = aI + b𝟏𝟏ᵀ` with `XᵀX = I` and `X ≠ ±I` is `±σ₅`,
`σ₅ = (2/5)𝟏𝟏ᵀ − I`; a real matrix that no relabelling of the five directions changes is of that form, so `±σ₅` are the
only orthogonal involutions besides `±1` that no relabelling changes; `(σ₅)_{tt} = −3/5`, `(σ₅)_{st} = 2/5`,
`σ₅² = I`; the step from the last-step direction `t` is the line `γ(x_t)`, `x_t = (2/5)𝟏 − e_t` the column of `σ₅`, of length one,
`γ(x_t)² = 1`; on the eighty states `U = (2/5)B − (3/5)R` and `UᵀU = I`.

Recognition: the radar echo of one step, `(3/5)² + 4(2/5)² = 1 = v² + 1/γ²` with `v = 3/5`, `γ = 5/4`. Uses
Props. 4, 26, P1, P2 (a), P3 (b).

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_29
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_29 :
    (∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 → HasSum (fun n => (excursionLaw n : ℂ) * z ^ n)
      (z ^ 4 * (1 + z) / (16 - 8 * z - 3 * z ^ 2 - 3 * z ^ 3))) ∧
    HasSum excursionLaw 1 ∧ HasSum (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) * excursionLaw n) 16 ∧
    (∑' n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * excursionLaw n) - (∑' n : ℕ, (n : ℝ) * excursionLaw n) ^ 2 = 156 ∧
    [excursionCount 4, excursionCount 5, excursionCount 6, excursionCount 7, excursionCount 8] = [20, 120, 300, 1200, 4740] ∧
    (∀ m, statLaw fP m = (∑ w ∈ excursions m, (cP w : ℝ)) / (5 * 4 ^ (m - 1))) ∧
    (∀ m, statLaw fQ m = (∑ w ∈ excursions m, (cQ w : ℝ)) / (5 * 4 ^ (m - 1))) ∧
    HasSum (statLaw fP) 10 ∧ HasSum (statLaw fQ) 5 ∧
    HasSum (statLaw fPP) 174 ∧ HasSum (statLaw fQQ) 32 ∧ HasSum (statLaw fPQ) 80 ∧
    varP = 84 ∧ varQ = 12 ∧ covPQ = 30 ∧ varP - covPQ ^ 2 / varQ = 9 ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), IsExcursion w → 1 + cP w + cQ w = w.length) ∧
    deriv (fun y => excursionF 1 1 y) 1 = excursionMean fP ∧ deriv (fun x => excursionF 1 x 1) 1 = excursionMean fQ ∧
    deriv (deriv (fun y => excursionF 1 1 y)) 1 = excursionMean fPP ∧
    deriv (deriv (fun x => excursionF 1 x 1)) 1 = excursionMean fQQ ∧
    deriv (fun x => deriv (fun y => excursionF 1 x y) 1) 1 = excursionMean fPQ
theorems.description:
**Proposition 29 (the excursion).** With `f_n` the excursions among the walks of length `n`, divided by `5·4ⁿ⁻¹`:
`F(z) = Σ f_n zⁿ = z⁴(1 + z)/(16 − 8z − 3z² − 3z³)` (for `|z| ≤ 1`); `F(1) = 1`, `Eℓ = F′(1) = Σ n f_n = 16`,
`Var ℓ = 156`; the excursions of length `4, …, 8` number `20, 120, 300, 1200, 4740`; with `P` and `Q` the symmetric and
the vector states an excursion meets, `E P = 10`, `E Q = 5`, `Var P = 84`, `Var Q = 12`, `Cov(P, Q) = 30`,
`Var P − Cov²/Var Q = 9`; an excursion of `ℓ` steps has `ℓ = 1 + P + Q`; and the derivatives of B.29's `F(z, x, y)` at
`(1, 1, 1)` are these moments.

Recognition: a walk comes back to the vertex of its start with chance one, in sixteen steps on average; an excursion
meets one of each of the fifteen two-spinor states other than the singlet on average. Uses Props. 24 to 26, P2 (a).

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_30
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_30_full :
    (∑ t, lineOnRel t) * (∑ t, lineOnRel t) = (5 : ℂ) • (1 : Matrix Two Two ℂ) ∧
    (∀ w : List (Fin 5), relOfWord w = 0 → relLine w = (coef w : ℂ) • Ω ∧ (coef w = 1 ∨ coef w = -1)) ∧
    (∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ ≤ 1 → HasSum (fun n => (signedLaw n : ℂ) * z ^ n) (-z ^ 4 / (16 + 3 * z ^ 2))) ∧
    [signedExcursionCount 4, signedExcursionCount 5, signedExcursionCount 6, signedExcursionCount 7, signedExcursionCount 8] =
      [-20, 0, 60, 0, -180] ∧
    (∀ n < 4, excursions n = ∅) ∧
    (excursions 4).card = 20 ∧ (∀ w ∈ excursions 4, coef w = -1 ∧ ∃ s t : Fin 5, s ≠ t ∧ w = [t, s, t, s]) ∧
    HasSum signedLaw (-1 / 19) ∧ HasSum (fun n => (signedLaw n : ℂ) * Complex.I ^ n) (-1 / 13) ∧
    ((∑' n, excursionLaw n) + (∑' n, signedLaw n)) / 2 = 9 / 19 ∧
    ((∑' n, excursionLaw n) - (∑' n, signedLaw n)) / 2 = 10 / 19 ∧
    ((∑' n, excursionLaw n) - (∑' n, signedLaw n)) / 8 = 5 / 38 ∧
    varP / (2 * (varP + varQ)) = 7 / 16
theorems.description:
**Proposition 30 (the signed excursion).** `A₋ = Σ_t γ_t ⊗ 1` on the sixteen two-spinor states has `A₋² = 5`; at the end of an
excursion the two-spinor state is `σ_w Ω`, `σ_w = ±1`; `Φ(z) = Σ_n zⁿ Σ_{excursions w, |w| = n} σ_w/(5·4ⁿ⁻¹) = −z⁴/(16 + 3z²)`; the
signed counts of the lengths `4, …, 8` are `−20, 0, 60, 0, −180`; no excursion is shorter than four, and the twenty
shortest excursions are the words `tsts` and come back with `−1`; `Φ(1) = −1/19`, `Φ(i) = −1/13`; an excursion keeps its sign
with chance `9/19` and reverses it with chance `10/19`, `a = (F(1) − Φ(1))/8 = 5/38`; and
`b = Var P/(2(Var P + Var Q)) = 7/16`.

Recognition: the sign `−1` of `tsts` is spin one half; the lean `10/19` toward reversal is attraction. Uses
Props. 4, 10, 24, 29.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_31
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_31_full (h : Fin 5) :
    (excursionStates h).card = 74 ∧ (∀ s : State, reach h 3 s = inExcursion h s) ∧
    (∀ k, 3 ≤ k → ∀ s : State, reach h k s = inExcursion h s) ∧
    (∀ s : State, Continues s (lastDirectionRel h, h) → s.1 = 0) ∧
    (∀ s' : State, inExcursion h s' → watchedIn64 h s' = 64) ∧
    (∀ s : State, inExcursion h s → watchedOut64 h s = 64) ∧
    alongCount h h = 60 ∧ (∀ j, j ≠ h → alongCount h j = 59) ∧ ∑ j, alongCount h j = 296 ∧
    (let M : ℚ := ∑ j, (alongCount h j : ℚ)
     let Ch : ℚ := alongCount h h
     let σ : ℚ := 5 * Ch / M
     let η : ℚ := 5 * 59 / M
     Ch / M = 15 / 74 ∧ σ = 75 / 74 ∧ η = 295 / 296 ∧ σ + 4 * η = 5 ∧ η / σ = 59 / 60 ∧
       σ - 1 = 4 * (1 - η) ∧ σ - 1 = 1 / 74 ∧ 6 * M + Ch = 1836) ∧
    ((excursionStates h).filter fun s => h ∉ disagreeSet s.1).card = 34 ∧ (34 : ℚ) / 74 = 17 / 37
theorems.description:
**Proposition 31 (the transitions of one excursion).** An excursion that begins at a moment whose last-step direction is `h` can be in
`80 − 5 − 1 = 74` states (the five `(∅, t)` end it; `(T_h, h)` is reached only from the start's vertex, by the
undo); they are exactly the states its steps reach, within four steps and for every number of steps from four on; the
uniform law on them is the stationary law of the steps watched on them (each state takes in and gives out the total
weight one); `M = 4·74 = 296` continuations, `C_h = 60` along `h` and `C_j = 59` along each other line;
`c_L = 15/74`, `σ = 75/74`, `η = 295/296`, `σ + 4η = 5`, `η/σ = 59/60`, `σ − 1 = 4(1 − η) = 1/74`; `34` of the `74`
leave `h` undivided, `R_ud = 17/37`.

Recognition: existing tilts a line toward its own direction by one part in `296`. Uses Props. 24, 26.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_32
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_32_full {X G : Type*} [Group G] :
    (∀ (c : Connection X G) (g : X → G) (x y : X), (c.rename g).U x y = g x * c.U x y * (g y)⁻¹) ∧
    (∀ (c : Connection X G) (g : X → G) (x : X) (rest : List X),
      (x :: rest).getLast (List.cons_ne_nil x rest) = x →
      hol (c.rename g) (x :: rest) = g x * hol c (x :: rest) * (g x)⁻¹) ∧
    (∀ {n R : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [CommRing R] (x : X) (rest : List X),
      (x :: rest).getLast (List.cons_ne_nil x rest) = x →
      IsFact (fun c : Connection X (Matrix n n R)ˣ =>
        ((hol c (x :: rest) : (Matrix n n R)ˣ) : Matrix n n R).trace)) ∧
    (∀ (c : Connection X G) (x : X) (rest : List X),
      (x :: rest).getLast (List.cons_ne_nil x rest) ≠ x →
      ∀ V : G, ∃ g : X → G, hol (c.rename g) (x :: rest) = V) ∧
    (∀ {α : Type*} (φ : G → α) (x : X) (rest : List X),
      (x :: rest).getLast (List.cons_ne_nil x rest) ≠ x →
      IsFact (fun c : Connection X G => φ (hol c (x :: rest))) → ∀ V W : G, φ V = φ W)

theorems.description:
**Proposition 32 (closed facts).** A gauge transformation takes `U_xy ↦ g_xU_xyg_y⁻¹`; the holonomy of a closed walk
at `x₀` turns by the gauge at its own vertex, `hol ↦ g_{x₀} hol g_{x₀}⁻¹`, so its trace is a fact (for every group of
invertible matrices over every commutative ring); the transport of an open walk from `x` to `y ≠ x` can be gauge-transformed
into every rotation, and only the constants are facts of it.

Recognition: Einstein's point coincidences and the gauge principle, with Wilson's closed loops. Uses P4,
Definition 24.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_33
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_33 {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommRing R] :
    (∀ v w : Fin n → R, SysExt.ιv v * SysExt.εv w + SysExt.εv w * SysExt.ιv v =
      (v ⬝ᵥ w) • (1 : Module.End R (Finset (Fin n) → R))) ∧
    (∀ v w : Fin n → R, SysExt.εv v * SysExt.εv w + SysExt.εv w * SysExt.εv v = 0) ∧
    (∀ v w : Fin n → R, SysExt.ιv v * SysExt.ιv w + SysExt.ιv w * SysExt.ιv v = 0) ∧
    (∀ v w : Fin n → R, SysExt.Jv v * SysExt.Jv w + SysExt.Jv w * SysExt.Jv v =
      (2 * (v ⬝ᵥ w)) • (1 : Module.End R (Finset (Fin n) → R))) ∧
    (∀ v : Fin n → R, SysExt.Jv v * SysExt.Jv v = (v ⬝ᵥ v) • (1 : Module.End R (Finset (Fin n) → R))) ∧
    (∀ (a : Fin n) (S : Finset (Fin n)), SysExt.Jx (R := R) a (Pi.single S (1 : R)) =
      SysExt.extSign (R := R) a (S.erase a) • (Pi.single (symmDiff S {a}) (1 : R) : Finset (Fin n) → R)) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin n), SysExt.ordProd (SysExt.Jx (R := R)) S (Pi.single ∅ 1) = Pi.single S 1) ∧
    (∀ (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R), Oᵀ * O = 1 →
      SysExt.extMap O * SysExt.extMap Oᵀ = 1 ∧ SysExt.extMap Oᵀ * SysExt.extMap O = 1 ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n → R, SysExt.extMap O * SysExt.Jv v * SysExt.extMap Oᵀ = SysExt.Jv (O *ᵥ v)) ∧
    (∀ a : Fin 6, Article.whole (A := Module.End ℂ (Finset (Fin 6) → ℂ)) (fun a => SysExt.εx a)
        (fun a => SysExt.ιx a) * SysExt.εx a =
      -(SysExt.ιx a * Article.whole (A := Module.End ℂ (Finset (Fin 6) → ℂ)) (fun a => SysExt.εx a)
        (fun a => SysExt.ιx a)))
theorems.description:
**Proposition 33 (the vertical step).** On the exterior algebra of `n` directions (the sixty-four sets at `n = 6`):
`ι(v)ε(w) + ε(w)ι(v) = ⟨v, w⟩`, `ε(v)ε(w) + ε(w)ε(v) = 0 = ι(v)ι(w) + ι(w)ι(v)`; `J(v) = ε(v) + ι(v)` has
`J(v)J(w) + J(w)J(v) = 2⟨v, w⟩` and `J(v)² = |v|²`; `J_a f_S = (−1)^{#\{s ∈ S : s < a\}} f_{S △ \{a\}}`;
`J_{s₁} ⋯ J_{s_r} f_∅ = f_{\{s₁,…,s_r\}}` (`s₁ < ⋯ < s_r`); `Λ(O) J(v) Λ(O)⁻¹ = J(Ov)` for every rotation `O`
(`Λ(O)⁻¹ = Λ(Oᵀ)`); and the step of the proof: the whole `w = J₀⋯J₅` turns adding into removing,
`w ε_a = −ι_a w`.

Recognition: dividing a direction and undividing it are one operation. Uses Definitions 13, 26, P3 (b).

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_34
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_34_full {n : ℕ} :
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → SysExt.Jx (R := ℝ) a * SysExt.Jx b * SysExt.Jx a * SysExt.Jx b = -1) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b →
      SysExt.Jx (R := ℝ) a (SysExt.Jx b (SysExt.Jx a (SysExt.Jx b (Pi.single (∅ : Finset (Fin n)) 1)))) =
        -Pi.single (∅ : Finset (Fin n)) (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → ∀ θ : ℝ,
      NormedSpace.exp ((θ / 2) • LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv' (SysExt.Jx (R := ℝ) a * SysExt.Jx b)) =
        LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv' (SysExt.rotor a b θ) ∧
      SysExt.rotor a b θ = Real.cos (θ / 2) • 1 + Real.sin (θ / 2) • (SysExt.Jx a * SysExt.Jx b)) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → ∀ θ : ℝ, SysExt.rotor a b θ * SysExt.rotor a b (-θ) = 1 ∧
      ∀ v : Fin n → ℝ, SysExt.rotor a b θ * SysExt.Jv v * SysExt.rotor a b (-θ) =
        SysExt.Jv (SysExt.planeRot a b θ *ᵥ v)) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, SysExt.rotor a b (2 * Real.pi) = -1 ∧ SysExt.planeRot a b (2 * Real.pi) = 1) ∧
    (∀ (D : Finset (Fin 6)) (x y : Fin 6),
      SysExt.halfStep D x * SysExt.halfStep D y + SysExt.halfStep D y * SysExt.halfStep D x =
        if x = y then (2 * thetaAt D x) • 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ (D : Finset (Fin 6)) (x y : Fin 6), x ≠ y →
      (SysExt.halfStep D x * SysExt.halfStep D y) * (SysExt.halfStep D x * SysExt.halfStep D y) =
        (-(thetaAt D x * thetaAt D y)) • 1) ∧
    (∀ D : Finset (Fin 6),
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 6 × Fin 6 => p.1 < p.2 ∧ (p.1 ∈ D ↔ p.2 ∈ D)).card =
        D.card.choose 2 + (6 - D.card).choose 2 ∧
      (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 6 × Fin 6 => p.1 < p.2 ∧ ¬(p.1 ∈ D ↔ p.2 ∈ D)).card =
        D.card * (6 - D.card)) ∧
    (∀ (D : Finset (Fin 6)) (x : Fin 5 ⊕ Fin 10), Kept D x ↔ ((plane x).1 ∈ D ↔ (plane x).2 ∈ D))

theorems.description:
**Proposition 34 (spin one half).** `J_aJ_bJ_aJ_b = −1` (`a ≠ b`): the loop `f_∅ → f_b → f_{ab} → f_a → f_∅`
comes back with `−1`; `R_ab(ϑ) = e^{ϑJ_aJ_b/2} = cos(ϑ/2) + J_aJ_b sin(ϑ/2)`, `R_ab(ϑ) J(v) R_ab(ϑ)⁻¹ = J(O_ϑ v)`
for every `v` (`O_ϑ` the rotation of the plane `(a, b)` by `ϑ`), and `R_ab(2π) = −1` while `O_{2π} = 1`; with the square
root of the sign of a division `D`, `f_x = i^{[x ∈ D]} J_x` has `f_xf_y + f_yf_x = 2θ_D(x)δ_xy` and
`(f_xf_y)² = −θ_D(x)θ_D(y)` (`x ≠ y`): `−1` on the `C(k,2) + C(6−k,2)` planes within a side and `+1` on the
`k(6−k)` planes across (`k = |D|`); and these are the division's kept and moved rotations: a rotation is kept exactly when its
plane lies within one side.

Recognition: spin one half, four quarter turns around a plane come back with `−1`; a loop across the division is a
boost and never closes. Uses Props. 21, 33, Definition 14.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_35
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_35 :
    SysExt.volume (R := ℂ) * SysExt.volume = -1 ∧
    (∀ D : Finset (Fin 6), (List.ofFn (SysExt.halfStep D)).prod = Complex.I ^ D.card • SysExt.volume) ∧
    (∀ D : Finset (Fin 6), SysExt.extMap (half D) (Pi.single Finset.univ 1) =
        (half D).det • Pi.single Finset.univ 1 ∧ (half D).det = Complex.I ^ D.card) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 6), SysExt.extMap (Complex.I • (1 : Matrix (Fin 6) (Fin 6) ℂ)) (Pi.single S 1) =
      Complex.I ^ S.card • Pi.single S 1 ∧ zS S = Complex.I ^ S.card) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 6), zS S ^ 2 = (theta ℂ S).det ∧ (theta ℂ S).det = (-1) ^ S.card) ∧
    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k → zS ∅ = 1 ∧ zS {0} = Complex.I ∧ zS {0, h.succ} = -1 ∧
      zS {h.succ} = Complex.I ∧ zS {h.succ, k.succ} = -1 ∧
      zS ((({h, k} : Finset (Fin 5))ᶜ).map (Fin.succEmb 5)) = -Complex.I) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 6), zS (symmDiff S {0}) = Complex.I * zS S ∨
      zS (symmDiff S {0}) = -Complex.I * zS S)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 35 (the phase of the whole).** `w = J₀J₁⋯J₅` has `w² = −1`; with the square root of the sign of `D`,
`f₀f₁⋯f₅ = i^{|D|} w`; `Λ(q_D) f_{\{0,…,5\}} = det(q_D) f_{\{0,…,5\}} = i^{|D|} f_{\{0,…,5\}}`;
`Λ(iI) f_S = i^{|S|} f_S`, `z_S = i^{|S|}`; `z_S² = det θ_S = (−1)^{|S|}`; `z_S = 1, i, −1, i, −1, −i` on the six
divided sets `{}, {n}, {h,n}, {h}, F, C` of a line; and `z_{S △ \{n\}} = ±i z_S`.

Recognition: the four phases `1, i, −1, −i`; counterparts differ by a quarter turn. Uses Props. 19, 27, 33, 34.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_36
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_36 {n : ℕ} {R : Type*} [CommRing R] :
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → SysExt.Tx (R := R) a b =
      ∑ k ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), SysExt.degreeProj k * (SysExt.Jx a * SysExt.Jx b) * SysExt.degreeProj k) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, SysExt.Nx * SysExt.Tx (R := R) a b = SysExt.Tx a b * SysExt.Nx) ∧
    (∀ a b c : Fin n, a ≠ b → b ≠ c → a ≠ c →
      SysExt.Tx (R := R) a b * SysExt.Tx b c - SysExt.Tx b c * SysExt.Tx a b = SysExt.Tx a c) ∧
    (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → a ≠ d → b ≠ c → b ≠ d →
      SysExt.Tx (R := R) a b * SysExt.Tx c d = SysExt.Tx c d * SysExt.Tx a b) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b →
      SysExt.Jx (R := R) a * SysExt.Jx b = SysExt.Tx a b + SysExt.εx a * SysExt.εx b + SysExt.ιx a * SysExt.ιx b) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → ∀ θ : ℝ,
      NormedSpace.exp (θ • LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv' (SysExt.Tx (R := ℝ) a b)) =
        LinearMap.toMatrixAlgEquiv' (SysExt.extMap (NormedSpace.exp (θ • unitTurn a b))))

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_37
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_37 {n : ℕ} {X : Type*} :
    (∀ (a : Fin n → ℝ) (U gx gy : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), gxᵀ * gx = 1 →
      SysExt.extMap gx * SysExt.jointStep a U * SysExt.extMap gyᵀ =
        SysExt.jointStep (gx *ᵥ a) (gx * U * gyᵀ)) ∧
    (∀ (c : Connection X (SysExt.Rot n)) (g : X → SysExt.Rot n) (a : Fin n → ℝ) (x y : X),
      SysExt.extMap (g x : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * SysExt.connStep c a x y *
          SysExt.extMap ((g y)⁻¹ : SysExt.Rot n) =
        SysExt.connStep (c.rename g) ((g x : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ a) x y) ∧
    (∀ (c : Connection X (SysExt.Rot n)) (a : Fin n → ℝ), a ⬝ᵥ a = 1 → ∀ x y : X,
      SysExt.connStep c a x y * SysExt.connStep c ((c.U y x : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ a) y x = 1 ∧
      SysExt.connStep c ((c.U y x : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ a) y x * SysExt.connStep c a x y = 1) ∧
    Function.Bijective SysExt.evenToFour ∧
    (∀ t : Fin 5, SysExt.evenToFour (SysExt.singletLine t) = (-Complex.I) • γ t) ∧
    (∀ s t : Fin 5, SysExt.evenToFour (SysExt.lineLine s t) = γ s * γ t) ∧
    SysExt.evenToFour wholeEven = (-Complex.I) • (1 : Matrix Four Four ℂ) ∧
    (wholeEven : CliffordAlgebra SysExt.Q6) =
      SysExt.cl 0 * SysExt.cl 1 * SysExt.cl 2 * SysExt.cl 3 * SysExt.cl 4 * SysExt.cl 5 ∧
    (∀ t : Fin 5, γ t = Complex.I • SysExt.evenToFour (SysExt.singletLine t)) ∧
    Function.Injective SysExt.stepRep ∧ (∀ a : Fin 6, SysExt.stepRep (SysExt.cl a) = SysExt.Jx a)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 37 (one step joins the two).** `𝒯 = J(a)Λ(U)` is gauge-transformed like one transport,
`Λ(g_x)𝒯_{xy}Λ(g_y)⁻¹ = J(g_xa)Λ(g_xU_{xy}g_y⁻¹)`, for every connection of P4 with values in the rotations of the six;
`𝒯_{xy}⁻¹ = J(U_{yx}a)Λ(U_{yx})` for a unit direction; on the four amplitudes the even words of the step are all the
operators (an isomorphism of real algebras from the even Clifford algebra of the six), with `J_nJ_t ↦ −iγ_t`,
`J_sJ_t ↦ γ_sγ_t`, `w ↦ −i`; so a step of one system along `t` is `γ_t = i J_nJ_t`, two vertical steps; the vertical
steps on the sixty-four sets are a faithful representation of the Clifford algebra of the six.

Recognition: the four amplitudes are the spinor of the six; the quantum `i` is the whole `w`. Uses Props. 4, 5, 33,
P4, Definitions 24, 26.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_38

    (∀ {n R : Type} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [CommRing R] (c : Connection (Fin 16) (Matrix n n R)ˣ)

theorems.description:
**Proposition 38 (curvature).** The curvature `F_st(x) = hol(x; tsts) − 1` turns under a gauge transformation by
the gauge at its vertex, `F_st(x) ↦ g_xF_st(x)g_x⁻¹`; every closed walk of four steps is a square `tsts`; ten
squares pass through each vertex and there are forty in all, which with the sixteen vertices build the cells of `ℝP⁴`
(SI Prop. 116, `Comparison.System.prop_116`); for `U_{xy} = e^{a_{xy}}` near one, with `a = (a₁, …, a₄)` the rotations
of the four steps in order, `hol = exp(Σ aᵢ + ½ Σ_{i>j}[aᵢ, aⱼ]) + O(‖a‖³)` uniformly for small rotations, that is
`log hol = Σ aᵢ + ½ Σ_{i>j}[aᵢ, aⱼ] + O(a³)`.

Recognition: the curvature is the force, `F = dA + A ∧ A` when the vertices are many and the rotations small. Uses
Props. 25, 32, Definition 25.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_39
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_39_full {n : ℕ} :
    (∀ (D : Finset (Fin n)) (X : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ),
      massForm D X X = ∑ i, ∑ j, ((X * projD D - projD D * X) i j) ^ 2 ∧ 0 ≤ massForm D X X ∧
      (massForm D X X = 0 ↔ X * thetaD D = thetaD D * X)) ∧
    (∀ (D : Finset (Fin n)) (a b : Fin n), a ∈ D → b ∉ D → massForm D (unitTurn a b) (unitTurn a b) = 2) ∧
    (∀ U Px Py gx gy : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, gyᵀ * gy = 1 →
      covDiff (gx * U * gyᵀ) (gx * Px * gxᵀ) (gy * Py * gyᵀ) = gx * covDiff U Px Py * gxᵀ) ∧
    (∀ Px Py : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
      (fun A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ => covDiff (NormedSpace.exp A) Px Py - ((Py - Px) + (A * Py + Py * Aᵀ)))
        =O[𝓝 0] fun A => ‖A‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ Px Py : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ,
      (fun A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ => covDiff (NormedSpace.exp A) Px Py - ((Py - Px) + (A * Py - Py * A)))
        =O[𝓝[{A | Aᵀ = -A}] 0] fun A => ‖A‖ ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ A Py : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, Aᵀ = -A → A * Py + Py * Aᵀ = A * Py - Py * A) ∧
    (∀ A Px Py : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, Aᵀ = -A →
      covDiff (1 + A) Px Py = (Py - Px) + (A * Py - Py * A) - A * Py * A) ∧
    (∀ U Px Py : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, U * Uᵀ = 1 →
      covDiffC U (qHalf Px) (qHalf Py) = (Complex.I - 1) • toC (covDiff U Px Py)) ∧
    (∀ M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ, frobSq ((Complex.I - 1) • toC M) = 2 * ∑ i, ∑ j, M i j ^ 2) ∧
    (∀ (D : Finset (Fin n)) (X : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ),
      frobSq ((Complex.I - 1) • toC (X * projD D - projD D * X)) = 2 * massForm D X X)

theorems.description:
**Proposition 39 (kept and moved: the mass form).** `M_D(X, X) = ‖[X, P_D]‖² ≥ 0`, zero exactly when `X` is kept;
`M_D = 2` on every unit moved rotation `E_ab − E_ba` (`a ∈ D`, `b ∉ D`); between neighbouring vertices
`DP_D = U_{xy}P_D(y)U_{xy}⁻¹ − P_D(x) ↦ g_x(DP_D)g_x⁻¹`; near one, `U = e^A`,
`DP_D = (P_D(y) − P_D(x)) + (AP_D(y) + P_D(y)Aᵀ) + O(‖A‖²)`, which along the rotations `Aᵀ = −A` is
`(P_D(y) − P_D(x)) + [A, P_D(y)] + O(‖A‖²)`, and for `U = 1 + A` exactly `(P_D(y) − P_D(x)) + [A, P_D(y)] − AP_D(y)A`; with `q_D = 1 + (i − 1)P_D`,
`Dq_D = (i − 1)DP_D` and `‖Dq_D‖² = 2‖DP_D‖²`; along a rotation `X`, `‖Dq_D‖² = 2M_D(X, X)`.

Recognition: the kept rotations are massless gauge fields and the moved rotations massive (Englert, Brout, Higgs). Uses
Prop. 21, Definitions 15, 27.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_91
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_91 :
    (∀ q : Fin 16 → Fin 16 → Circle, (∀ x y, q y x = (q x y)⁻¹) →
      ((∃ z : Fin 16 → Circle, ∀ x y, clebsch.Adj x y → z x = q x y * z y) ↔
        ∀ (u : Fin 16) (p : clebsch.Walk u u), ArticleStatements.Clock.walkProd (fun x y => q y x) p = 1)) ∧
    clebsch.Preconnected ∧
    (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin 16 × Fin 16 => p.1 < p.2 ∧ Adjacent p.1 p.2).card = 40 ∧

theorems.description:
**Proposition 91 (the common clock).** Phases `q_{xy} = q_{yx}⁻¹` in `U(1)` on the forty links of the sixteen
vertices have a common phase, `z_x = q_{xy}z_y` on every link, exactly when the product of `q` around every closed walk
is one (the vertices being connected); the flat sign `q ≡ −1` closes every square with `(−1)⁴ = +1` and the closed
walk `12345` with `(−1)⁵ = −1`, so it has no common phase; the centre of the kept rotations has dimension `0, 0, 1, 0`
at the types `0|6, 1|5, 2|4, 3|3` (and their complements), at `2|4` the rotation of the two-direction part, which at the
plane `F = \{h, k\}` is the action of the plane's rotation `γ_hγ_k` on the six.

Recognition: the common time of electromagnetism; the field is the obstruction to it, which the Aharonov–Bohm phase
measures; the flat sign is the loop of `ℝP⁴`. Uses Props. 25, 38, 41, Definition 28.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_40
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_40_full (h k : Fin 5) (hhk : h ≠ k) :

    (∀ S ∈ sixOf h k, ∀ a b : Fin 6, a ∈ S → b ∉ S → massForm S (unitTurn a b) (unitTurn a b) = 2) ∧
    (∀ S ∈ sixOf h k, ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Fin d → Matrix (Fin 6) (Fin 6) ℂ)
        (dA : Fin d → Fin d → Matrix (Fin 6) (Fin 6) ℂ) (μ ν : Fin d),

    (sixOf h k).map divLines = [∅, Finset.univ, Finset.univ.erase h, {h}, {h, k}, Finset.univ \ {h, k}] ∧
    (∀ S ∈ sixOf h k, Geometry.realFormAlg (Geometry.projOf S) =

        X.trace = 0 ∧ X * (gammaD (divLines S) * Comparison.J) = (gammaD (divLines S) * Comparison.J) * X.map star) ∧
      ∀ v : Four → ℂ, Cop (divLines S) (Cop (divLines S) v) = (countSign (divLines S).card : ℂ) • v) ∧
    countSign 1 = -1 ∧ countSign 3 = 1 ∧ countSign 5 = -1 ∧

    (∀ S ∈ sixOf h k, ∀ v w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (6 - S.card)) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin S.card),
      v ≠ 0 → ‖v.1‖ = ‖v.2‖ → w ≠ 0 → ‖w.1‖ = ‖w.2‖ →

      v ≠ 0 → ‖v.1‖ = ‖v.2‖ → 0 < ‖v.1‖ ∧ ‖(GroupsContinuumLaw.nrmPQ v).1‖ = 1 ∧ ‖(GroupsContinuumLaw.nrmPQ v).2‖ = 1)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 40 (the table of the six).** For every last-step direction `h` and plane `{h, k}`, the six divisions a line holds,
`{}`, `{n}`, `{h, n}`, `{h}`, `F = {h, k}`, `C`, have: the types `0¦6, 1¦5, 2¦4, 1¦5, 2¦4, 3¦3`; the time-like
part (the smaller part, where `θ_S = −1`): none, the singlet, the singlet and `h`, the last-step direction, the plane, none; the loops
`−1/+1`: `15/0, 10/5, 7/8, 10/5, 7/8, 6/9` (a loop `(f_xf_y)²` is `−1` within a side, `+1` across); the phases
`z_S = 1, i, −1, i, −1, −i`; kept/moved of the fifteen `15/0, 10/5, 7/8, 10/5, 7/8, 6/9` and of the ten
`10/0, 10/0, 6/4, 6/4, 4/6, 4/6`, counterparts keeping the same ten; a centre of the kept rotations of dimension
`0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0`, the clocks `E_{n h} − E_{h n}` at `{h, n}` and `E_{h k} − E_{k h}` at `F` (the rotations of `iγ_h`
and `γ_hγ_k`, Prop. 41); every moved unit rotation has `M_S = 2`; for every connection the curvature splits as
`A = A_k + A_m`, `F_k = F(A_k) + (A_m ∧ A_m)_k`, `F_m = D_{A_k}A_m` (the derivatives of the parts are the parts of
the derivative, `keptPart_hasFDerivAt`, `movedPart_hasFDerivAt`); the rows divide the lines `∅`, all five, all but
`h`, `{h}`, `{h, k}`, `C`, and the real form of each row (Definition 15) is the real span of fifteen generators,
`{X : tr X = 0, X†h_D + h_DX = 0}` for the even line sets `D` (`h_D` Hermitian, `h_D² = 1`, trace zero for
`|D| = 2, 4`) and `{X : tr X = 0, XC_D = C_DX}` for the odd ones (`C_D² = −1, −1, +1` at `|D| = 1, 5, 3`); the
balanced directions of each row are the `v ≠ 0` with `|v off S| = |v on S|`, and two of them span one line exactly
when their normalized representatives agree up to sign: the balanced lines are `(S^{5−k} × S^{k−1})/ℤ₂`, `k = |S|`.
The real forms as groups (`SU(4)`, `SU*(4)`, `SU(2,2)`, `SL(4, ℝ)`) are in the geometry layer.

Recognition: `{}` the universality of gravity; `{n}` the sign of time of every pair and the sphere of lines; `{h}`
the ten rotations split at the last-step direction, `6 + 4`, spin connection and co-frame; `{h, n}` the line's own clock; `F` the common
time and light; `C` two times and no clock, colour; the real forms `su(4)`, `sl(2, ℍ)`, `su(2,2)`, `sl(4, ℝ)` and the
balanced directions `S⁴`, `(S¹ × S³)/ℤ₂`, `(S² × S²)/ℤ₂`. Uses Props. 21, 22, 27, 34, 35, 39, Definitions 15, 28.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_41
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_41 (h k : Fin 5) (hhk : h ≠ k) :

theorems.description:
**Proposition 41 (the clock of a line, and its mass).** `iγ_h` is the clock of `{h, n}`: it is kept, it
commutes with every rotation `{h, n}` keeps, it turns the plane `(n, h)` of the six (as `−2(E_{n h} − E_{h n})`), whose
unit rotation is a clock and spans the centre of the kept rotations; at `{h}` it is moved;
`e^{iaγ_h} = cos a + i sin a γ_h`, `(e^{iaγ_h} ⊗ e^{iaγ_h})Ω = cos 2a Ω + sin 2a iℓ_h`, `e^{i(π/2)γ_h} = iγ_h`;
`γ_hγ_k` (the plane's rotation, `±γ_hγ_k`) is the clock of `F = {h, k}`: kept, commuting with every rotation `F` keeps, its
unit rotation spans the centre; and it is moved at `{h}` and at `{k}`.

Recognition: the line's own time and its rest mass are one rotation, de Broglie's internal clock, `E = mc²`; the plane's
clock is the common time, the conformal time translation of `SU(2,2)`. Uses Props. 17, 21, 40, Definition 28.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_42
theorems.statement:
theorem prop_42 :

       else gen x * (gammaD (divLines S) * Comparison.J) =

      (∀ v v' w : Four → ℂ, star (Cop (divLines S) (v + v')) ⬝ᵥ w =

      (∀ v w w' : Four → ℂ, star (Cop (divLines S) v) ⬝ᵥ (w + w') =

      (countSign (divLines S).card = -1 ↔ ((divLines S).card = 1 ∨ (divLines S).card = 5)) ∧
      (countSign (divLines S).card = 1 ↔ (divLines S).card = 3) ∧

    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 6), zS S = (half S).det ∧ zS S ^ 2 = (theta ℂ S).det ∧
      (Even S.card → (theta ℂ S).det = 1) ∧ (Odd S.card → (theta ℂ S).det = -1)) ∧
    (∀ S : Finset (Fin 6), (twin S).card % 2 ≠ S.card % 2)
theorems.description:
**Proposition 42 (count and amplitude).** For every divided set `S` of the six, read with the singlet undivided as the
division of the lines `D = divLines S` (`|D| ≡ |S|` mod 2): the rotations `S` keeps are exactly those that commute with
`γ_D` (`|S|` even) or with the antilinear `C_S = γ_DΘ` (`|S|` odd); for `S` even the kept form
`h_S = i^{r(r−1)/2}γ_D` is Hermitian and `⟨v, h_S v⟩` is real, a count; for `S` odd, `⟨C_S v, w⟩` is linear in `v`
and in `w`, an amplitude, `C_S² = s_r`, `⟨C_S v, w⟩ = s_r ⟨C_S w, v⟩` (antisymmetric where `C² = −1`, `r = 1, 5`;
symmetric where `C² = +1`, `r = 3`), and `⟨C_S v, C_S u⟩ = ⟨u, v⟩`, so `|⟨C_S v, w⟩|²` is a chance between two
states; `z_S = det q_S`, `z_S² = det θ_S`, `+1` for `S` even and `−1` for `S` odd; and a counterpart has the other parity.

Recognition: a count is a probability, an amplitude a transition amplitude; matter is counted, its counterpart with `n` added is a
quantum amplitude. Uses Props. 7, 19, 35, the Lemma of the divisions (the section on divisions), Definition 29.

theorems.name: Comparison.System.prop_43

    (∀ h k : Fin 5, h ≠ k →

      dividedSet (relOfWord [h, k]) = {h.succ, k.succ} ∧ twin {h.succ, k.succ} = outside h k) ∧
    (∀ a b : Fin 5, a ≠ b → ∀ r : Fin 16, disagreeSet r = {a, b} →
      dividedSet r = {a.succ, b.succ} ∧ twin {a.succ, b.succ} = outside a b) ∧

theorems.description:
**Proposition 43 (where each piece sits).** An excursion closes the two-spinor state of a line to itself, the singlet, whose
divided set is `{}`, with the counterpart `{n}`; a step along `t` makes `ℓ_t`, divided set `{t, n}`, counterpart `{t}`; for every last-step direction `h`
and plane `{h, k}` of a line (Prop. 27: `r_{k,k} = Ω`, `r_{k,k−1} = ℓ_h`, `r_{k,k−2} = ±e_{hk}`), the three two-spinor states
have the divided sets `{}`, `{h, n}`, `{h, k}` and the counterparts `{n}`, `{h}`, `C` (the three lines outside the plane); every
symmetric state `e_{ab}` has the divided set `{a, b}` and the counterpart `{a, b}'`, the three lines outside it; every divided set is
even (a count, Prop. 42) and its counterpart with `n` added odd (an amplitude).

Recognition: `{}` carries gravity, the proton and the cosmos; `{n}` sizes and moments; `{t, n}` the step; `{t}`
colour per vertex and `α_s`; `{h, n}` the clock and the weak contact; `{h}` the Higgs; `F` the electric plane and
light; `C` the strong force; `{a, b}` the leptons and `{a, b}'` the quarks. Uses Props. 27, 42, Definition 29.

    (∀ t : Fin 5, Law.LS {t.succ} = 3 ∧ Law.wS {t.succ} = I / 3 ∧ Law.eS {t.succ} = 1 / 3) ∧

theorems.description:
**Proposition 44 (the step at each divided set).** On the five directions, with `q_S` the square root of the sign of the divided set:
`G_S = q_S†q_S = 1` (`S` even), `G_S = q_Sᵀq_S = θ_S` (`S` odd); `L_S = 𝟏ᵀG_S𝟏 = 5` (`S` even), `5 − 2k` (`S` odd,
`k` lines in `S`), never `0`; the coin at `S`, `σ_S = (2/L_S)𝟏𝟏ᵀG_S − I`, has `σ_S² = I` and `σ_∅ = σ₅`, Prop. 28's
coin; the reflection is `1 − 2/|L_S|` and the weight of a step `w_S = z_S/L_S`; at an even divided set `|w_S| = 1/5`; a symmetric
state continues once to a vector state and three times to symmetric states when its last-step direction is in the plane, twice and twice when
it is not; of the `200` departures from the fifty symmetric states `80` reach a vector state, `120` a plane and `12` each
plane: transmission `2|w_S| = 2/5 = 80/200`, reflection `1 − 2|w_S| = 3/5 = 120/200`, `s = 12/200 = 3/50` per plane; at
`{t}`: `L = 3`, `w = i/3`, reflection `1/3`; at `{n}`: `L = 5`, reflection `3/5`; at the counterpart of a plane named by its three
outside lines `L = −1`, `w = i`, named `{n, a, b}` `L = 1`, `w = −i`; `w² = −1` either way.

Recognition: the reflection `3/5` of the counted step gives `f = (3/5)²/10`, the reflection `1/3` of the coherent one
`α_s² = (1/3)²/8`. Uses Props. 19, 28, 29, 35, 42.

theorems.description:
**Proposition 97 (the reflections are radar steps).** `tanh log 2 = 3/5`, `tanh(log 2/2) = 1/3`,
`tanh(log 2/4) = 3 − 2√2 = tan²(π/8)`, `cosh log 2 = 5/4`; the reflection at every even divided set is `tanh log 2` and at a
line alone `tanh(log 2/2)` (Prop. 44); `tan²(π/8)` is the half phase of the line factor at the last-step direction's phase
(Prop. 51).

Recognition: the reflection of a counted step is the speed of one radar step of rapidity `log 2` (`v = 3/5`, `γ = 5/4`);
the reflection of a step carried as an amplitude halves that rapidity, and the half phase of the line factor quarters it.
Uses Props. 44, 51.

theorems.description:
**Proposition 45 (one generation, seen from the plane).** For every plane `F = {h, k}`: each two-spinor state `e_S`
meets the plane in `N_F = |S ∩ F|` lines and the outside in `N_C = |S ∩ C|`, `N_F + N_C = |S| ∈ {0, 2, 4}`; the
classes `(N_F, N_C) = (0,0), (2,0), (1,1), (0,2), (1,3), (2,2)` hold `1, 1, 6, 3, 2, 3` two-spinor states, with
`Y = N_F/2 − N_C/3 = 0, 1, 1/6, −2/3, −1/2, 1/3`; `Y = Σ_{x ∈ S} y_x` with `y = ½` on the plane and `−⅓` outside,
`Σ_x y_x = 0`; the values of `Y` occur `1, 6, 3, 1, 3, 2` times; `Σ Y = Σ Y³ = 0`, the colour and the doublet sums of
`Y` vanish, as many two-spinor states in triplets as in antitriplets, eight in doublets; `Σ Y⁵ = 5/9`;
`Q = N_k − N_C/3 = T₃ + Y`, `T₃ = (N_k − N_h)/2`, with the charges `0` twice, `2/3, −1/3, −2/3, 1/3` three times,
`±1` once; the last-step direction's vector state is neutral; the ten symmetric states meet `F` in two lines once, in one line six times, in
none three times.

Recognition: with the line charges `(0, 1, −⅓, −⅓, −⅓)` the sixteen two-spinor states are `ν^c` (`Y = 0`), `e^c` (`1`),
`u^c` (`−2/3`, three), `Q` (`1/6`, six), `d^c` (`1/3`, three) and `L` (`−1/2`, two): one generation with its
right-handed neutrino; the vanishing sums are the absence of anomalies; the eight two-spinor states meeting the plane in one
line are the weak doublets, parity broken at the plane. Uses Props. 10, 25.

theorems.description:
**Proposition 46 (the rotations of a pair, and what each keeps).** The ten lines of a pair on `H ⊗ H ⊗ ℂ²`,
`Γ_a = γ_a ⊗ 1 ⊗ σ_x`, `Γ_{5+a} = 1 ⊗ γ_a ⊗ σ_y`, anticommute, `Γ_xΓ_y + Γ_yΓ_x = 2δ_xy`; the two-spinor states are
`σ_z = +1`, on which the rotations `½Γ_xΓ_y` act as `γ_aγ_b ⊗ 1`, `1 ⊗ γ_aγ_b` and `iγ_a ⊗ γ_b` (times `½`); they are
`so(10)`: `M ↦ ρ(M) = ¼ Σ M_xy Γ_xΓ_y` keeps the commutator and is injective on the antisymmetric `M`, dimension
45; `−i Σ_t Γ_tΓ_{5+t} = (L − 1) ⊗ σ_z` and `e^{−iπL/4} = −iP` (as an operator, and on each two-spinor state); the rotations
keeping the comparison are `u(5)`: `Z ↦ ρ([[Re Z, −Im Z], [Im Z, Re Z]])` is an injective real-linear map of Lie
algebras from the anti-Hermitian `5 × 5` matrices onto them, 25 (keeping `L ⊗ 1` likewise), with centre
`ℝ·i(L − 1) ⊗ σ_z`, the rotation `ρ(J) = ½ i(L − 1) ⊗ σ_z` of the complex structure; keeping also the singlet `Ω ⊗ e₊`:
`tr Z = 0`, `su(5)`, 24; keeping also the plane count `N_F = Σ_{t ∈ F}(1 − (γ_t ⊗ γ_t) ⊗ σ_z)/2`: `Z` in
`s(u(3) ⊕ u(2))`, 12, with centre `ℝ·ρ(iY)`; keeping also the last-step direction's two-spinor state `ℓ_h ⊗ e₊`: `Z` in `su(3) ⊕ u(1)`, 9,
with centre `ℝ·ρ(iQ)` — at every plane `F = {h, k}` with the last-step direction `h` (`Z` read after a relabelling `π` with
`π 3 = h`, `π 4 = k`; `Y = ½` on `F`, `−⅓` on `C`; `Q = 0` on `h`, `1` on `k`, `−⅓` on `C`);
`(A, B, z) ↦ (z²A, z̄³B)` maps `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)` onto `S(U(3) × U(2))`, with kernel the six images of the sixth
roots of unity, cyclic, and `(SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1))/ℤ₆ ≃ S(U(3) × U(2))`; and on the sixteen, at every plane,
`Tr Y = Tr Y³ = 0` and the colour and the doublet sums of `Y` vanish (`Tr YT_c² = Tr YT₃² = 0`).

Recognition: the gauge group of the standard model, `S(U(2) × U(3)) = (SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1))/ℤ₆`, twelve
generators, held by `SU(5)`; `Y` the hypercharge, `Q` the electric charge. Uses Props. 4, 10, 11, 45.

theorems.description:
**Proposition 47 (the last-step direction).** The mass form of the division of a real line is `M_h(X, Y) = 2⟨Xh, Yh⟩`, on
`ℂ⁵ = ℝ¹⁰` `M_v(X, Y) = 2 Re⟨Xv, Yv⟩` for anti-Hermitian `X`, `Y`, so `M_v(X, X) = 2|Xv|²`, and `½M_v` is the
Gram `Re⟨Xv, Yv⟩`; for every plane `F = {h, k}` and every unit vector `v`
of `F`: thirteen rotations that span `u(3) ⊕ u(2)` (the anti-Hermitian matrices with no entry across `F`), orthonormal
for `Re tr(X†Y)`, on which `½M_v(X_i, X_j) = Re⟨X_iv, X_jv⟩ = diag(1, 0, ½, ½, 0, …, 0)`: three of thirteen move
the last-step direction, `w_h = 3/13`, `χ_h = w_h(1 − w_h) = 30/169`; and twelve orthonormal rotations that span `s(u(3) ⊕ u(2))`, on
which the form has `det(x − G) = x⁹(x − ½)²(x − 4/5)`: `½M_v = 4/5, ½, ½, 0⁹`; `(½)/(4/5) = 5/8`,
`sin²θ = 1 − 5/8 = 3/8`.

Recognition: the last-step direction moves `W⁺`, `W⁻` and `Z` (`½, ½, 4/5`); nine stay massless, the photon and the eight colour
rotations; the last-step direction's length is the Higgs scalar; at the source `M_W²/M_Z² = 5/8`, `sin²θ_W = 3/8`. Uses Props. 21, 39,
46, Definition 27.
